extracted.intended_audience: public water system owners/operators and State drinking water program officials (lead and copper rule implementers)
extracted.subtask_short: OCCT compliance for public water systems
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and evaluation criteria for optimizing or re-optimizing optimal corrosion control treatment (OCCT) under the Lead and Copper Rule for public water systems, including study, designation, installation, monitoring, and State oversight steps and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: State authority to require re-optimization for small systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may require a small water system that does not have to re-optimize under paragraphs (a)(3)(i)(A) through (C) of this section to re-optimize under § 141.82(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives States discretion to require re-optimization even where federal triggers would not. Applies to small systems; notification and process per § 141.82(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger: service line replacement completion and subsequent exceedance
rubrics_metrics.description: After completing service line replacement in accordance with the requirements in § 141.84(d) and there are no lead, galvanized requiring replacement, or lead status unknown service lines remaining in the inventory, if at the end of a subsequent tap sampling period, the system exceeds the lead action level, a small water system with corrosion control treatment must meet the requirements under paragraph (d) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion of mandatory service line replacement does not eliminate obligations if a later tap sampling period shows exceedance; triggers re-optimization requirements for small systems with corrosion control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger: systems without corrosion control exceeding action levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Small and non-transient non-community water systems without corrosion control treatment that exceed either the lead action level or copper action level must complete the corrosion control treatment steps specified in paragraph (e) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of corrosion control treatment plus exceedance mandates following the (e) treatment steps and timelines (study, designation, install, monitor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed OCCT by consecutive tap monitoring (no corrosion control)
rubrics_metrics.description: A medium water system without corrosion control treatment or a small water system is deemed to have OCCT if the water system does not exceed the lead action level and copper action level during two consecutive six-month tap monitoring periods and then remains at or below the lead action level and copper action level in all tap sampling periods conducted in accordance with § 141.86.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility restrictions: small systems with corrosion control treatment are not eligible for this paragraph where the State has set OWQPs under paragraph (d) or (e). If such a system later exceeds action levels it must follow paragraph (a) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed OCCT by 90th percentile ≤ lead PQL and copper compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system is deemed to have optimized or re-optimized corrosion control treatment if it submits tap sampling results demonstrating the 90th percentile lead level is ≤ lead practical quantitation limit of 0.005 mg/L for two consecutive six-month tap monitoring periods, it does not exceed the copper action level for two consecutive six-month tap monitoring periods, and it does not have OWQPs designated by the State under paragraph (d) or (e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a system later exceeds the lead PQL or copper action level it is not eligible to be deemed optimized until it completes treatment steps in paragraph (d) or (e). Systems deemed under this paragraph must monitor at least once every three calendar years using reduced sites (§ 141.86(d)(1)) and prescribed times/locations (§ 141.86(d)(2)(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation submission to State for deemed OCCT
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must submit documentation of meeting the applicable requirements to the State in accordance with § 141.90(c)(1) by the applicable deadline for submitting tap sampling results under § 141.90(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative requirement: timely submission of evidence to claim 'deemed OCCT' status per referenced sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systems with OCCT must continue treatment and meet State additional requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A system with corrosion control treatment deemed to have OCCT must continue to operate and maintain the corrosion control treatment and also meet any additional requirements that the State determines are appropriate to ensure OCCT is maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State may impose additional terms to ensure maintenance of OCCT even after a system is 'deemed' optimized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 (re-optimization/optimization): initiate mandatory pipe rig/loop or CCT study or treatment recommendation (timelines vary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems with corrosion control treatment required to re-optimize under paragraph (a) must initiate studies or recommend treatment options: (i) large/medium systems with lead service lines that exceed the lead action level must harvest lead service lines and construct flowthrough pipe rigs/loops and operate them with finished water within one year after the end of the tap sampling period in which they exceeded the lead action level; (ii) large systems without lead service lines that exceed lead or copper action levels must conduct corrosion control studies; (iii) other systems must recommend re-optimized OCCT within six months after the end of the tap sampling period in which the system exceeded action levels; (iv) systems may make existing treatment modification recommendations within six months after the end of the tap sampling period in which the system exceeded the lead action level, subject to State evaluation and timelines for State specification and installation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 1 establishes immediate study or recommendation obligations, with specific harvesting/pipe rig requirements for systems with lead service lines and allowed paths for existing treatment modifications (State evaluation required).

rubrics_metrics.name: State may require CCT study or designate re-optimized OCCT (Step 2) with deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one year after the end of the tap sampling period in which a medium water system without lead service lines or a small system exceeded the lead action level or copper action level, the State may require the water system to perform corrosion control studies for re-optimization. If the State does not require such studies, the State must specify re-optimized OCCT within timeframes: for a medium water system, within one year after the end of the tap sampling period; for a small water system, within 18 months after the end of the tap sampling period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State must provide written determination to the system and has discretion to require studies or instead specify re-optimized OCCT within stated deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study duration deadlines (Step 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any water system with lead service lines that exceeds the lead action level must complete the pipe rig/loop corrosion control treatment studies and recommend re-optimized OCCT within 30 months after the end of the tap sampling period in which the system exceeded the lead action level. If required to perform other corrosion control studies, systems must complete studies and recommend re-optimized OCCT within 18 months after the end of the tap sampling period in which the system exceeded the lead or copper action level or after the State requires such studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinct study-duration deadlines depending on presence of lead service lines and whether pipe rig/loop studies are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: State designation of re-optimized OCCT within six months after study completion (Step 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The State must designate re-optimized OCCT within six months after the water system completes the study duration (paragraph (d)(3)(i) or (ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State decision timeline to act on study results and designate re-optimized OCCT; State notification must be in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-optimized OCCT installation deadlines (Step 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems must install re-optimized OCCT within one year after the State completes Step 4 or completes Step 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Installation deadlines after State designation: typically one year for re-optimized OCCT (for systems with existing corrosion control treatment), subject to referenced paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up monitoring requirement after installation (Step 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems must complete standard monitoring for at least two consecutive tap monitoring periods under § 141.86(c)(2)(iii)(D) and water quality parameter monitoring under § 141.87(b)(3) after completing installation. The first tap monitoring period for standard monitoring must begin on January 1 or July 1, whichever is sooner, after completing installation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow-up monitoring confirms effectiveness; schedules anchored to Jan 1 or Jul 1 after installation completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: State sets OWQPs after follow-up monitoring (Step 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The State must review the water system's re-optimized OCCT and designate optimal water quality parameters (OWQPs) within six months after completing follow-up monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OWQPs are set based on post-installation monitoring results to define operating targets for maintaining OCCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systems must meet OWQPs and continue sampling (Step 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems must comply with State-designated OWQPs and conduct tap sampling under § 141.86(c)(2)(iii)(E) and water quality parameter monitoring under § 141.87(b)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing compliance requires maintaining parameters within State-designated ranges and continuing required monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimization steps and timelines for systems without corrosion control treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems without corrosion control treatment must complete analogous steps (initiate studies/recommendations, State may require studies, study durations, State designation, installation, follow-up monitoring, State sets OWQPs, systems meet OWQPs) with some different timelines: State must notify medium systems within 18 months and small systems within 24 months if it does not require studies; OCCT installation deadlines are within 24 months after State designation; study durations may be 30 months for large/medium with lead service lines and 18 months for others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This parallels the re-optimization pathway but uses the paragraphs in (e) and has longer installation deadlines (24 months) for systems newly installing OCCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five‑year-or‑less service line replacement deferment eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system with one or more lead or galvanized requiring replacement service lines is not required to complete the steps under paragraph (d) or (e) if the system meets all the following requirements: (i) complete service line replacement under § 141.84(d) in five years or less from the relevant exceedance (with special rule for large systems without corrosion control whose trigger is the lead PQL), (ii) replace at minimum the total number of lead/galvanized lines each year at an annual rate equally divided by the total number of years provided (not to exceed five years), (iii) by the end of the period must have replaced all calculated lines, identified materials for unknowns, completed inventory validation per § 141.84(b)(5), and replaced unknowns found to be lead/galvanized requiring replacement, and (iv) comply with all other § 141.84(d) requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows deferment of CCT steps when full service line replacement can be completed quickly; requires strict annual pacing, inventory validation, and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual replacement rate, reporting, and loss of deferment consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must replace the minimum annual number of lead/galvanized requiring replacement service lines each year as identified in inventory, and if they fail to meet the minimum annual rate in any year of the five‑year-or‑less period or fail to complete replacement requirements, they must meet the requirements under paragraph (d) or (e) starting immediately after failure. At the end of each year of the period, the system must submit written documentation to the State about the number removed and whether the minimum annual replacement rate was met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual reporting to State is required; failure to meet pace cancels deferment and triggers immediate CCT pathway obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five‑year completion does not preclude later CCT steps if later exceedance
rubrics_metrics.description: After completing service line replacement in accordance with paragraph (f), a water system must meet the requirements under paragraph (d) or (e), as applicable, if at the end of a subsequent tap sampling period, the system either exceeds the lead action level or the lead practical quantitation limit, whichever is applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completing replacement is not a permanent exemption — later exceedances require following CCT steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for small/medium systems without treatment that achieve two consecutive compliant six‑month periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Any small or medium water system without corrosion control treatment required to complete the steps in paragraph (e) that does not exceed the lead action level and copper action level during two consecutive six‑month tap monitoring periods prior to the start of step 3 or prior to or concurrent with the end of step 4 may stop completing the steps and is not required to complete paragraph (e)(3) or (5), except medium systems with lead service lines must complete the study under paragraph (e)(3)(i). A 90th percentile at or below action levels based on less than the required minimum number of samples cannot be used. Eligible systems can use this exception only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a 'stop early' exception but with strict sampling-count requirements, one-time use only, and continued obligations for some medium systems with lead service lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to complete remaining steps once step 5 is started
rubrics_metrics.description: Any system that starts step 5 must complete all remaining steps (i.e., steps 6 through 8) in paragraphs (e)(6) through (8) and is not permitted to stop the steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once installation step begins, the system must follow through with follow-up monitoring and OWQP designation and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resumption requirement if exception-used system later exceeds action levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Any small or medium water system without corrosion control treatment that stopped the steps under paragraph (e) and subsequently exceeds either the lead action level or copper action level must complete the corrosion control treatment steps in paragraph (e) beginning with the first treatment step that was not completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a system previously used the early-stop exception and later has an exceedance, it must resume the unfinished steps from where it left off.

rubrics_metrics.name: State may require repetition of previously completed treatment steps
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may require a water system to repeat treatment steps previously completed by the water system when the State determines that this is necessary to implement the treatment requirements of this section. The State must notify the system in writing of such a determination and explain the basis for its decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State discretion to demand repetition for adequacy; written notice and rationale required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirement for upcoming long‑term change in treatment or source
rubrics_metrics.description: At a time specified by the State, or if no specific time is designated, as early as possible but no later than six months prior to the addition of a new source or any long-term change in water treatment, a water system must submit written documentation describing the addition of a new source or long-term change in treatment to the State. Systems may not implement the addition without State approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State review and approval is required before implementing long-term changes; State may require additional monitoring, tap sampling, and re-evaluation of corrosion control treatment. Examples include switching disinfectants, coagulants, inhibitor products, or dose changes planned to alter finished water pH or inhibitor concentration. Short-term daily fluctuations are not 'long-term changes.'

rubrics_metrics.name: System recommendation regarding corrosion control treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any system without corrosion control treatment required to recommend a treatment option must, based on lead/copper tap sampling and water quality parameter monitoring, recommend designating one or more of the corrosion control treatments listed in paragraph (c)(1) to the State as the OCCT. Any system with corrosion control treatment that exceeds the lead action level and is required to recommend must recommend treatments listed in paragraph (c)(2). The State may require additional monitoring to review the recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations must be data-driven and may prompt State requests for further monitoring. States may waive the recommendation requirement if they require a CCT study within 3 months after the exceedance, in which case the system proceeds directly to paragraph (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: State discretion to require CCT studies to identify OCCT or re‑optimized OCCT
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may require any small or medium water system without corrosion control treatment that exceeds action levels to perform corrosion control treatment studies under paragraph (c)(1) to identify OCCT. The State may require any small or medium water system with corrosion control treatment that exceeds action levels to perform corrosion control treatment studies under paragraph (c)(2) to identify re-optimized OCCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State may demand studies for small/medium systems; requirement applies to both initial optimization and re-optimization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required treatments to evaluate in CCT studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems without corrosion control treatment must evaluate the effectiveness of: (i) alkalinity and pH adjustment; (ii) addition of an orthophosphate- or silicate-based corrosion inhibitor at a concentration sufficient to maintain an effective inhibitor residual in all test samples; (iii) orthophosphate to maintain 1 mg/L (as PO4) residual in all test samples; and (iv) orthophosphate to maintain 3 mg/L (as PO4) residual in all test samples. Systems with corrosion control treatment must evaluate similar options (alkalinity/pH adjustment or re-adjustment; addition of inhibitor if none is used; orthophosphate at 1 mg/L and 3 mg/L unless current process already meets these residuals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All specified strategies must be evaluated individually or in combination; some residual targets are conditional on current treatment status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study methods: pipe rig/loop, metal coupon, partial‑system tests, or analogous analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must evaluate each treatment option individually or in combinations using pipe rig/loop tests, metal coupon tests, partial-system tests, and/or analyses based on documented analogous treatments with similar size systems that have similar water chemistry and distribution configurations. Large/medium systems with lead service lines must conduct pipe rig/loop studies using harvested lead service lines to assess effectiveness on existing pipe scale. Metal coupon tests can be used as a screen to reduce options evaluated in pipe rig/loop studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies allowable test methods and requires harvested lead pipes for rig/loop studies where applicable; metal coupon tests are screening tools but cannot replace required studies when rig/loop is mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required water quality parameters to measure in CCT tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must measure the following in any tests conducted: (i) Lead; (ii) Copper; (iii) pH; (iv) Alkalinity; (v) Orthophosphate as PO4 (when orthophosphate-based inhibitor is used); (vi) Silicate (when a silicate-based inhibitor is used); and (vii) Any additional parameters necessary to evaluate effectiveness as determined by the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameters must be measured both before and after evaluating treatments; additional parameters may be required by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and documentation of chemical or physical constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must identify all chemical or physical constraints that limit or prohibit the use of a particular corrosion control treatment and document those constraints by providing either: (i) data showing a treatment has adversely affected other drinking water treatment processes when used by another comparable system; or (ii) data showing the water system previously attempted evaluation and found the treatment ineffective or adversely affecting other processes. Systems using metal coupon tests or pipe rig/loop studies cannot exclude strategies from studies based on these identified constraints (with narrow exception if previously found ineffective in a pipe rig/loop study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must provide empirical documentation to justify excluding treatments; prior ineffective findings in a pipe rig/loop study allow exclusion; screening tests cannot be sole basis for exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate effect of corrosion control chemicals on other treatment processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must evaluate the effect of the chemicals used for corrosion control treatment on other drinking water quality treatment processes. Systems using metal coupon tests to screen and/or pipe rig/loop studies to evaluate treatment options cannot exclude any of the required treatment strategies specified in paragraph (c)(1) or (2) from the studies based on the effects identified in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interference with other processes must be evaluated and documented but cannot be used to exclude required strategies from study unless supported as in constraints documentation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to State with rationale and supporting documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on data and analysis for each treatment option evaluated, systems must recommend to the State, in writing, the treatment option that the corrosion control studies indicate constitutes OCCT for that system. Systems must provide the State with a rationale for the OCCT recommendation and all supporting documentation specified in paragraph (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written recommendation must include data, analysis, constraints, and justification to support the proposed OCCT designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: State designation of OCCT or re-optimized OCCT with written explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on available information including studies and/or a system's recommended option, the State must either approve the system's recommended option or designate alternative corrosion control treatment(s) from among those listed, and must notify the water system in writing of its designation and explain the basis for this determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State decision must be documented and can select among listed strategies; State must consider effects of additional treatment on water quality parameters and other treatment processes and may request additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Install and operate designated OCCT throughout distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Each system must install and operate the OCCT or re-optimized OCCT designated by the State throughout its distribution system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational requirement: full distribution installation and ongoing operation consistent with State designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: State review and designation of OWQPs (pH, orthophosphate/silicate, alkalinity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The State must evaluate lead/copper tap and water quality parameter sampling and determine: (1) a minimum value or range for pH at each entry point; (2) a minimum pH in all distribution samples, equal to or greater than 7.0 unless not feasible or necessary; (3) if a corrosion inhibitor is used, a minimum concentration or range for orthophosphate (as PO4) or silicate at each entry point; (4) if an inhibitor is used, a minimum orthophosphate or silicate concentration in all tap samples necessary to form a passivating film (with orthophosphate minimums: ≥0.5 mg/L PO4 for systems previously without corrosion control, ≥1.0 mg/L PO4 for systems previously with corrosion control unless State determines otherwise); (5) if alkalinity is adjusted, a minimum concentration or range for alkalinity at entry points and in tap samples; and (6) State may designate values for additional parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OWQPs set explicit operating targets (including numeric orthophosphate minima for specified situations) and must be communicated in writing with the basis for decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued operation and monitoring for OCCT with six‑month compliance assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: All systems must continue to operate and maintain OCCT, including maintaining water quality parameters at or above minimum values or within ranges designated by the State for all water quality parameter samples collected under § 141.87(b)(4). Compliance must be determined every six months; a system is out of compliance for a six‑month period if it has excursions for any State-specified parameter on more than nine days, cumulatively, during the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires ongoing maintenance and semiannual compliance checks using the excursion-days metric; States may exclude obvious sampling errors from calculation but must record them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily value calculation rules for water quality parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Daily value rules: (i) On days with more than one measurement at a sampling location, daily value is the average of all results collected that day (regardless of continuous monitoring, grab sampling, or combo), unless EPA-approved alternative formula in State program revision applies; (ii) On days with only one measurement, daily value is that measurement; (iii) On days with no measurement, daily value is the daily value calculated on the most recent day when the parameter was measured at that location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how to aggregate multiple measurements and handle missing days; allows State-approved alternative aggregation formulas if EPA-approved in program revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: State may modify OCCT or OWQPs upon request or initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon its own initiative or in response to a written request by a water system or other interested party (explaining why modification is appropriate and providing supporting documentation), a State may modify its determination of OCCT or optimal water quality parameters. The State may require a CCT study to support modification and may modify its determination where necessary to ensure continued optimization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an administrative path for adjustment of State determinations; requests must be documented and State may demand additional study evidence.
